 Cornell football coach Dawson: a ‘welcoming guy’ who cared about the kids
 By Joe Napsha 4 Min Read 
 • Oct. 24, 2026 
 | 37 seconds ago 
-->
 Go Ad-Free today 
 Cornell head coach Ed Dawson. (Chaz Palla | TribLive) 
 Cornell High School football coach Ed Dawson is being remembered as “a great coach and a better man.”
 Dawson died after suffering a medical emergency during a game at Rochester on Friday night.
 Dawson, the veteran head coach of the Cornell football team, was “a welcoming guy … with a big personality” who cared about the players not only on his team, but the other team as well, said Donnie Militzer, coach at Our Lady of Sacred Heart, a Cornell rival. But the rivalry on the field did not affect their friendship.
 “It just crushed me,” Militzer said , adding he had heard about Dawson’s death from some OLSH students who perform in Cornell’s band.
 Militzer said that Dawson was deeply involved in Cornell’s football program — from the youth program to the high school players.
 Fort Cherry coach Tanner Garry said Dawson was a mentor to him in his first years as Fort Cherry coach.
 “He was a mentor, a leader and exemplified what a coach should be, on and off the field. He was a great friend and a great leader,” Garry said.
 “The best thing about him was that he was the ultimate coach and teacher. He coached hard and loved (his players),” said Freedom coach Ron Balog, whose team held preseason scrimmages with Cornell.
 Balog echoed Militzer’s sentiments about how Dawson cared about all of the players — including his opponent’s players.
 “He was a great soul and a great high school coach,” Balog said. “He put the kids first.”
 Cornell Superintendent Aaron Thomas said in a statement Friday that Dawson experienced a medical emergency on the sideline during the game and was transported to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
 “This is an extremely difficult situation. To say Coach Dawson was an integral part of Cornell School District would be an understatement,” Thomas said in the statement. “It is hard to put into words what Coach Dawson means to Cornell and we are all heartbroken, crushed and in shock.”
 Bill Sacco, Cornell athletic director, said Dawson told an assistant coach he was not feeling well during the second quarter Friday night and was advised to sit down on the bench. Dawson ended up lying down on the team bench. The game was called at that point with Cornell leading 16-6.
 Sacco said discussions will take place with “everyone, including Coach Dawson’s wife, to see if she feels we should go on.”
 Dawson took over as head coach of Cornell, which serves Coraopolis and Neville Island, in 2011. Due to low numbers of players, Cornell had a co-op football program with Quaker Valley, which is across the Ohio River in Sewickley. During that time, Dawson served as an assistant coach and liaison for Cornell on the Quaker Valley team.
 Cornell’s football program was revived in 2016; his team won a conference championship in 2019.
 Cornell entered play Friday night 3-5 overall and 1-4 in the Big 7 Conference, clinging to hope for a playoff berth.
 “He was a guy who always got the most out of his players,” Fort Cherry’s Garry said.
 “There will be discussions with a large group of people deciding what the next step will be,” Sacco said. “It will be a hard one no matter what step we take.
 “Cornell will grieve for a long time. We lost a great guy,” Sacco said. “I am not sure how we will get back to where we need to be.”
 In 2018, Dawson, a former star at Aliquippa who was part of Aliquippa state champion team, was one of the finalists for the head coaching job with the Quips to replace Mike Zmijanac as coach. The Aliquippa School Board selected Mike Warfield, another former star at Aliquippa.
 Balog said he coached Dawson’s son, E.J. Dawson, when he was playing quarterback. Dawson is a senior defensive lineman at Marietta College in Ohio, according to the team roster.
